column1: Why store generated embeddings instead of regenerating them for every similarity comparison?
column2:
To reuse vectors without another embedding-model call.
Similarity queries can compare the stored vectors directly.
Review source

column1: Why regenerate a stored embedding when the text it represents changes?
column2:
To keep similarity results aligned with the current source text.
Changing text alone does not recalculate a normal stored vector column.
Review source

column1: What must happen to separately stored embeddings when their source document is deleted?
column2:
Remove or invalidate the document's embeddings.
Otherwise, similarity search can return content that no longer exists in the source.
Review source

column1: How can a DML trigger schedule embedding refresh without generating vectors during the write?
column2:
Mark inserted or updated rows for a background worker.
The trigger still adds work to the write transaction.
Review source

column1: What must a separate worker handle when Microsoft Foundry supplies the embedding model?
column2:
Detect source changes and update the database's stored vectors.
Model hosting does not automatically synchronize an embeddings table.
Review source

column1: What freshness cost comes with asynchronous batch refresh of embeddings?
column2:
Search can use outdated vectors until the next successful refresh.
Choose a refresh frequency that meets the application's latency requirements.
Review source

column1: How does an Azure Functions SQL trigger detect rows needing embedding refresh?
column2:
By polling SQL Change Tracking.
The function can run model calls outside the database engine.
Review source

column1: Why can an unfiltered embedding-generation UPDATE be expensive?
column2:
It targets every row, including rows with current embeddings.
Use a filter to limit model calls to selected rows.
